text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bosnia's collective presidency failed to sign World Bank contract for $30 million loan due to disagreement among presidency members. World Bank officials astonished at delay.
- Momcilo Krajisnik, Serb member of collective presidency, openly confirms political strategy of Bosnian Serbs - a weak Bosnia and a very strong Serb republic, commentary says.
- Rasim Kadic, Bosnia's federation minister for refugees, says conditions for return of refugees from Germany to Bosnia have not been created yet and appeals for repatriation to be postponed.
- Fate of disputed town of Brcko is already decided. The town will be placed under three to five year international protectorate, unnamed sources tell newspaper.

- Sarajevo's wood-processing company Sipad Sumaprojekt presents 100 small and medium-sized wood processing projects backed by Italian partner company C.E.M.A. Impianti. Company says projects will be implemented in three to six months.

- An International Monetary Fund assistance programme for Bosnia cannot be realised without a common monetary policy and formation of a central bank. Without the IMF programme, international donors will be reluctant to offer substantial financial assistance, says IMF representative. -- Sarajevo
